newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Singapore, Malaysia relations normalising - Anwar.
newsitem.headline: Singapore, Malaysia relations normalising - Anwar.

text.p: Malaysian Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Sunday that while the basic issue in Malaysia's recent spat with Singapore has been settled, it will take time for relations to return to normal.

"I believe the issue is quite settled," Anwar told Reuters Financial Television, but he added that: "I think it has to be given some time. I don't think we should rush into a situation and ignore the sentiment of the Malaysian public."
"Notwithstanding that I think we have started normalising relations."
The two sometimes testy neighbours had a fresh falling out in March over a statement by Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew.

Lee described Johor Baru, a Malaysian city just across a short causeway from Singapore, as a dangerous place rife with crime. The comments sparked diplomatic and public protests in Malaysia and calls for a freeze in relations.
Anwar said Malaysia had accepted a later retraction by Lee Kuan Yew.
"What we have said is that any bilateral relations should be based on the principle of reciprocity," Anwar said.
He was in Cebu for a meeting of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum finance ministers.
